Synopsis

Strand Life Sciences, backed by Reliance Industries, is focused on expanding its CancerSpot screening test capabilities. The company seeks to lower the testing cost significantly over the next two years, targeting below ₹10,000. Reliance's goal includes making advanced diagnostics accessible to a larger population in India. Achieving this requires innovation and development of local genomic capabilities in technology and reagents.

Listen to this article in summarized format

Mumbai: Reliance Industries-backed Strand Life Sciences is targeting a major share of India’s potential market for early cancer detection over the next five years, as it looks to scale its proprietary blood-based CancerSpot screening test beyond its initial clinical validation.

The company estimates a Rs 2,600 crore addressable opportunity at just 5% adoption, based on an eligible population of about 52 million people aged 50-75.

In an independent validation cohort from Strand’s 1,480-participant case-control study, CancerSpot demonstrated 72% cancer detection sensitivity and a 1.4% false-positive rate. The underlying research was published in the peer-reviewed Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.

CancerSpot is intended to complement standard-of-care cancer screenings.

Reliance’s mandate for Strand is to dramatically bring down the cost of early-stage cancer and genomic testing, making advanced diagnostics more accessible in India. Strand is working towards bringing the cost of a test below Rs 10,000 (compared with Rs 26,000 now) over the next two years and Rs 1,000 in the long term, with lower-cost reagents, operational efficiencies and scale among the levers, chief executive Ramesh Hariharan said.

Reliance executive Nilesh Modi said achieving scale will require not only continued innovation but also the development of indigenous capabilities in genomic sequencing technologies, equipment and reagents. “This is a kind of Jio-fication of genomics and that is something we need to do by bringing down the cost so that more people can have access to it,” he added.

“India has the opportunity to build globally competitive capabilities in this critical space, while addressing the growing need for affordable and accessible cancer diagnostics,” Modi said.

Reliance acquired the Bengaluru-based company for Rs 393 crore in 2021. The conglomerate is leveraging Strand Life Sciences for its entry into the emerging areas of specialised healthcare diagnostics and genomic sciences.

Genomic tests are based on blood or saliva samples or tissues extracted from the body. Such tests are gaining traction, helping understand the risks of diseases, how cancers progress, guide personalised plans for targeted therapies, and in distinguishing inherited traits like genes, proteins, or chromosomes that affect individual well-being.

Cancer cells shed DNA into the blood with a different methylation pattern from healthy cells. CancerSpot, which is applicable across 14 cancer types like lung, liver, kidney and stomach, reads that pattern and uses AI to detect whether a cancer signal is present.

“Strand is committed to the mission of democratising genomics through innovation, developing affordable solutions and expanding access to advanced genomic testing, ultimately enabling better and more timely cancer care,” said Hariharan.

Indigenisation, scale, automation and miniaturisation are the levers that will help bring the cost down.
